LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen about a third from its high — unusual for a defense contractor whose order book is still full — even though nothing about steady military spending has really changed.

ASML.sentence: ASML has pulled back a bit, but that's a normal dip within a long climb — they're still the only company in the world making the machines that print the most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet — the world's biggest industrial gas supplier is chugging along on long-term contracts, and interestingly the market isn't giving this top-quality operator any premium at all.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm with just a mild dip — the Azure cloud and AI story keeps grinding along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher had a good week as money starts flowing back into biotech research, which tends to show up in their lab-equipment orders a couple of quarters later.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge ticked up and keeps doing its steady toll-road thing moving oil and gas, though it's paying a fair rather than exceptionally generous dividend right now.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow bounced this week and has actually been outperforming its peers lately, even though it's still well below its high — big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its AI workflow tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore slipped a little and is lagging behind copper prices lately, which sometimes sets it up to catch back up to the metal it mines.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta is roughly flat; the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping up, and a headline dip in average pricing is just an accounting quirk from its lime acquisition, not real weakness.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA barely moved — the Latin American Coke bottler is benefiting from a strong Mexican peso, which lifts its earnings when converted to dollars, though the peso is near the strong end of its range.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras rose with high oil prices and pays big dividends right now, but its earnings look like they're near the top of the cycle, so there's some risk they roll over from here.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, had a strong week and is trading for less than its own ships would cost to replace — a sign the market is pricing it cheaply.

MA.sentence: Mastercard slipped slightly and is currently priced no higher than Visa, even though it's the faster-growing of the two — meanwhile people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical-robot maker is roughly flat but down sharply from its high, sitting at one of its cheaper points in years even as hospitals keep using its machines for more operations.
